title: A Cipher for the Ledger
premise: Ada Oyelaran has spent a decade as the night dispatcher for Marrow Creek Taxi, quietly cataloguing the town's confessions, lies, and midnight fares in her ledger. When twin letters arrive — one confessing to the drowning of Danny Voss twelve years ago, one promising that 'the rest is filed where you'd file it' — Ada realizes the cipher hidden in her own dispatch logs points to a killer still riding her routes. As the anniversary dinner approaches and the town closes ranks around its founding families, Ada must decode the ledger, confront the found family of drivers who raised her, and expose the truth even when it indicts the man who gave her belonging. The case closes at the anniversary dinner itself, where Ada reads the final entry aloud and the town's glass finally shatters.
about_author: Ulyana Joubert is the pen name of a former small-town radio operator who spent seven years logging night calls before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about the people who keep records — dispatchers, clerks, archivists — and the secrets they're forced to keep.

chapters.title: The Night Book
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A routine shift establishes her ritual: every fare, every odd call logged in her green ledger. We meet the drivers she considers family — gruff Ozzie, motherly Renata, quiet Teo. Emotional beat: comfort in order, and a flicker of loneliness beneath it.

chapters.title: Twin Envelopes
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Two letters arrive in the same mail drop: one unsigned confession to Danny Voss's drowning, one reading only 'the rest is filed where you'd file it.' Her hands shake as she logs them anyway. Emotional beat: dread cracking open her ordered world.

chapters.title: Where You'd File It
chapters.summary: Ada searches her decade of ledgers for the date of Danny's death and finds a fare she never questioned: a pickup from the reservoir road at 2:14 a.m., paid cash, passenger unnamed. Emotional beat: the horror that the answer was always in her hands.

chapters.title: Closed for Good
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Ada's POV. Twelve years ago: the town's verdict on Danny Voss — accident, alcohol, case closed by Sheriff Brandt himself. Young Ada believed it because everyone kind to her said so. Emotional beat: loyalty as a kind of blindness.

chapters.title: Ozzie Knows Something
chapters.summary: Ada probes Ozzie over coffee; he deflects with old-driver war stories but his eyes go to the ledger rack. She notices page 214 of the oldest book has been razored out. Emotional beat: suspicion entering the family home.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Committee
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Town matriarch Corliss Havel recruits Ada to manage transport for the twelfth-anniversary dinner honoring the Voss family's generosity — an event Danny's death nearly canceled. Emotional beat: being trusted by power for the first time, and hating what it might cost.

chapters.title: Fare 4471
chapters.summary: Ada cross-references the reservoir fare against dispatch tapes archived in the station basement. The tape exists — until she returns an hour later and it doesn't. Someone has keys. Emotional beat: hunted in her own territory.

chapters.title: Teo's Silence
chapters.summary: Teo, the youngest driver and closest to Ada, goes pale when she mentions the letters. He begs her to let it go, then refuses to say why. Emotional beat: the first fracture in her found family.

chapters.title: Renata's Rosary
chapters.summary: Renata's POV. The veteran driver prays over a bus token from the reservoir route, revealing to readers she drove someone home that night and has carried it silently since. Emotional beat: guilt worn as devotion.

chapters.title: The Cipher Emerges
chapters.summary: Ada maps the letters' phrasing against her log entries and finds a pattern: initials, times, zone codes spelling a name across ten years of mundane fares. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling into fear — the writer knows her system intimately.

chapters.title: Sheriff Brandt's Warning
chapters.summary: Brandt summons Ada, warns her off 'reopening grief,' and reveals he knows about the letters before she tells him. Emotional beat: realizing the confession was sent to more than one person — or that he's watching her.

chapters.title: Zone Six at Midnight
chapters.summary: Ada stakes out the reservoir road on a slow shift, dispatching herself a phantom fare. She finds fresh flowers on the bank and a second missing ledger page tucked under a stone. Emotional beat: communion with the dead boy no one mourned properly.

chapters.title: What the Page Says
chapters.summary: The recovered page shows three fares that night, not one — including a return trip an hour later with a soaked passenger. Ada decodes the initials: C.H. Emotional beat: vertigo; the town's beloved matriarch's name in her own hand.

chapters.title: Corliss's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Ada accepts Corliss's dinner invitation to study her. Corliss is warm, sharp, generous — and quotes a phrase from the second letter verbatim. Emotional beat: charm as camouflage; Ada leaves smiling and terrified.

chapters.title: Family Meeting
chapters.summary: Ada calls an emergency driver meeting to ask who else received letters. Ozzie slams the table; Renata cries; Teo walks out. Emotional beat: the found family fracturing under the weight of a secret none will name.

chapters.title: The Second Letter's Promise
chapters.summary: A third letter arrives: 'One more entry, then I'm done. Anniversary night.' Ada realizes the writer plans a public reveal — or a public execution of blame. Emotional beat: racing the clock.

chapters.title: Danny's Sister Returns
chapters.summary: Nadia Voss arrives in town to plan the dinner, brittle and beautiful, testing everyone's condolences. She asks Ada, oddly, whether the taxi company keeps records. Emotional beat: two keepers of memory recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Ozzie's Debt
chapters.summary: Ozzie's POV. He recalls the night he picked up Corliss Havel's son Miles, drunk and shaking, and took the fall for a dented fender without asking questions. Emotional beat: loyalty as complicity, decades deep.

chapters.title: Miles Havel
chapters.summary: Ada investigates Miles, now a semi-estranged heir living two towns over, and finds his alibi for the night — a rehab stay — checks out perfectly. Too perfectly. Emotional beat: the obvious suspect dissolving.

chapters.title: The Basement Tapes
chapters.summary: Ada discovers the stolen tape wasn't destroyed but copied; a duplicate sits in Teo's locker. Confronting him, she learns he was the dispatcher trainee on duty that night and was made to erase the original. Emotional beat: betrayal and pity entwined.

chapters.title: Who Made Teo Erase It
chapters.summary: Teo confesses under pressure: Brandt ordered the erasure, calling it 'closing the wound.' But Teo kept a copy because he couldn't live with it. Emotional beat: cowardice and conscience sharing one body.

chapters.title: Listening
chapters.summary: Ada and Teo play the tape: Danny alive at pickup, arguing with someone whose voice is half-drowned by static — but the dispatcher's log notation, in young Teo's hand, records the destination: the Havel boathouse. Emotional beat: the past speaking plainly at last.

chapters.title: Nadia's Ledger
chapters.summary: Nadia reveals she received a letter too — hers names a date and a fare number. Comparing notes, they realize the letter-writer is feeding each of them pieces, orchestrating rather than confessing. Emotional beat: alliance formed between the dead boy's blood and his record-keeper.

chapters.title: The Writer's Hand
chapters.summary: Ada analyzes the handwriting and typing quirks against years of memos and work orders. The looped descenders match one person: Renata. Emotional beat: devastation — the gentlest member of her family.

chapters.title: Renata Breaks
chapters.summary: Renata admits writing the letters but swears she didn't kill Danny: she saw something that night driving Corliss home, and has been dying of it for twelve years. She gives Ada the last piece — a key to the Havel boathouse. Emotional beat: confession as release, not solution.

chapters.title: The Boathouse
chapters.summary: Ada and Nadia search the boathouse and find Danny's jacket, weighted and rotting in a skiff, plus Corliss's husband Aldous's old ledger of payments to Brandt. Emotional beat: physical proof surfacing like a body.

chapters.title: Aldous Havel's Death
chapters.summary: Research reveals Aldous died eight months after Danny — officially a heart attack — right after demanding the case be closed. Ada wonders if Corliss buried two men. Emotional beat: the scale of the cover-up widening.

chapters.title: Brandt's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ada confronts Brandt with the payment ledger. He offers her a deal: silence, a promotion, protection — and hints darkly that Ozzie's pension and Teo's future hang on her cooperation. Emotional beat: temptation weaponizing her love for her found family.

chapters.title: What Belonging Costs
chapters.summary: Alone at the switchboard, Ada weighs the offer against everything the ledger means to her. She replays Danny's final call — logged as a distress fare she never answered because Corliss had her rerouted. Emotional beat: guilt crystallizing into resolve; this is personal now.

chapters.title: The Reroute Order
chapters.summary: Ada finds the original reroute slip — signed by Corliss, routed through the taxi company's owner, who turns out to be a Havel shell company. The company Ada gave her life to was bought to control its records. Emotional beat: her sanctuary was the crime scene all along.

chapters.title: Ozzie Chooses
chapters.summary: Ada tells Ozzie everything. After a long silence, he hands her the razored page he stole years ago to protect Renata — it names Corliss as the reservoir pickup. Emotional beat: the family choosing truth over loyalty, together.

chapters.title: Corliss Counterstrikes
chapters.summary: Corliss, warned by Brandt, moves first: Teo is fired for the erased tape, Renata's immigration status is threatened, and the anniversary dinner is recast as a tribute to the Havels' charity. Emotional beat: power showing its teeth.

chapters.title: Night Shift Siege
chapters.summary: Someone ransacks the dispatch office hunting the ledgers. Ada, forewarned, has already moved them — all forty books — to Nadia's motel room. Emotional beat: the keeper out-keeping her hunters.

chapters.title: The Full Cipher
chapters.summary: Ada and Nadia assemble the complete decoded sequence across twelve years: payments, silences, the reroute, the boathouse, Aldous's death. Every entry corroborated twice. Emotional beat: the ledger becoming a prosecution.

chapters.title: Anniversary Eve
chapters.summary: The town dresses up; Corliss rehearses her toast; Brandt stations officers at the doors. Ada decides she won't leak to press or sheriff — she'll read the entries aloud where the whole town can't look away. Emotional beat: terrible calm before the storm.

chapters.title: The Toast
chapters.summary: Climax begins. Corliss raises her glass to memory and mercy. Ada stands, ledger in hand, and asks the room to hold their glasses — she has an entry to read. Emotional beat: a single voice against a roomful of complicity.

chapters.title: Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Ada reads the cipher entries chronologically — the fare, the reroute, the boathouse, the payments — while Corliss's composure cracks and Brandt moves to arrest her. Nadia plays the tape over the hall speakers. Emotional beat: catharsis; the town hearing its own heartbeat exposed.

chapters.title: Corliss Unbound
chapters.summary: Corliss breaks — not screaming but precise, explaining Danny's blackmail over Aldous's crimes and the accidental shove, the cover-up that devoured her husband and her soul. Brandt is taken too. Emotional beat: monster revealed as a woman built by secrets.

chapters.title: After the Glass Shatters
chapters.summary: Fallout: the taxi company reverts to the drivers as a cooperative; Ozzie retires content; Teo is reinstated; Renata begins visiting Danny's grave with Nadia's forgiveness. Emotional beat: grief shared becomes belonging earned.

chapters.title: Entry One, New Ledger
chapters.summary: Ada opens a fresh green ledger and logs her first fare honestly, fully, no codes. On the shelf behind her, the old volumes wait as testimony. Final beat: she finally belongs — to the truth, and to the family that chose it with her.
